A gene set is a named list of genes that share a pathway or function, such as "oxidative
phosphorylation". Set-level tests ask whether a set's proteins move together. This step decides set
membership once, for every set-level analysis in the repository: which protein stands for each
gene, which sets are tested, and which genes each set holds in this experiment.

## Packages

GSEABase reads the GO Slim file and GO.db supplies the Gene Ontology hierarchy; both are called
with `::` where used.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
```

## Inputs

The protein list comes from the normalised matrix, so membership never depends on a fold change.
Two fixed snapshots sit in `references/` (sources in `references/README.md`):

- MSigDB release 2026.1.Hs, saved from msigdbr. It supplies Hallmark, Reactome, KEGG Legacy and GO
  Biological Process (GO:BP) membership. Membership shifts between releases, so the release is read
  from the snapshot, not from the installed package.
- The GO Consortium's generic GO Slim, a short list of broad GO terms.

```{r}
#| label: inputs
out <- here("01_Processing", "04_Gene_Sets", "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(
  proteins = "01_Processing/02_Normalisation/c_data/DAList_normalized.rds",
  msigdb = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/references/msigdb_2026.1.Hs.rds",
  goslim = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/references/goslim_generic.obo"
)
paths <- map_chr(inputs, here)
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
proteins <- readRDS(paths[["proteins"]])
msigdb <- readRDS(paths[["msigdb"]])
collections <- msigdb$collections
membership <- rename(msigdb$membership, collection = database)
msigdb$db_version
count(distinct(membership, set_id, collection), collection)
```

## One protein per gene

Set tests need one row per gene symbol. A protein with no symbol, or with several, is dropped
rather than split. When two proteins share a symbol, the one observed in the most runs represents
it, then the one with more peptides (`n_seq`), then the lower accession. The rule reads detection
only, never a fold change.

```{r}
#| label: protein-map
protein_map <- proteins$annotation |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(
    uniprot_id, n_seq,
    n_obs = rowSums(!is.na(proteins$data))[uniprot_id],
    gene = trimws(gene),
    mapping_status = case_when(
      is.na(gene) | !nzchar(gene) ~ "missing_symbol",
      grepl("[;,|]", gene) ~ "multiple_symbols",
      TRUE ~ "candidate"
    ),
    gene = if_else(mapping_status == "candidate", gene, NA_character_)
  )
representatives <- protein_map |>
  filter(mapping_status == "candidate") |>
  arrange(gene, desc(n_obs), desc(n_seq), uniprot_id) |>
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  pull(uniprot_id)
```

Plot labels need to be unique, so a symbol shared by two proteins gets its accession appended.

```{r}
#| label: labels
protein_map <- protein_map |>
  mutate(
    selected = uniprot_id %in% representatives,
    mapping_status = case_when(
      selected ~ "representative",
      mapping_status == "candidate" ~ "duplicate_gene",
      TRUE ~ mapping_status
    ),
    label = if_else(
      is.na(gene), uniprot_id,
      if_else(duplicated(gene) | duplicated(gene, fromLast = TRUE),
        paste0(gene, " (", uniprot_id, ")"), gene
      )
    )
  )
gene_map <- filter(protein_map, selected)
gene_universe <- gene_map$gene
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(protein_map$label))
mapping_summary <- count(protein_map, mapping_status, name = "n_proteins")
mapping_summary
```

In this data every protein carries one symbol of its own, so all of them represent their gene and
the duplicate and missing-symbol rules remove nothing. The gene universe, the genes this experiment
can speak to, holds `r length(gene_universe)` genes.

## Which MSigDB sets are tested

Each set is cut down to the genes measured here. A set qualifies when its source size is 15 to 500
genes and at least 15 of them were measured. 15 to 500 is the GSEA software's default range, and the
manuscript uses the same bounds. Size is the only filter before testing: no set is dropped for
overlapping another or for its name.

```{r}
#| label: msigdb-sets
set_members <- distinct(membership, set_id, gene)
sets_full <- split(set_members$gene, set_members$set_id)
sets_measured <- map(sets_full, intersect, y = gene_universe)

set_catalog <- membership |>
  distinct(set_id, collection, pathway, source_id, description) |>
  mutate(
    source_size = lengths(sets_full)[set_id],
    measured_size = lengths(sets_measured)[set_id],
    qualifies = source_size >= 15 & source_size <= 500 & measured_size >= 15
  )
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(set_catalog$set_id))
sets <- sets_measured[set_catalog$set_id[set_catalog$qualifies]]
stopifnot(length(sets) > 0)
set_catalog |>
  filter(collection == "Hallmark") |>
  select(pathway, source_size, measured_size, qualifies) |>
  head(5)
```

## GO Slim sets

GO terms form a hierarchy, and a broad term covers every narrower term beneath it. Each GO Slim
term becomes a set holding every measured gene annotated to it or to any term below it. The genes
come from the full MSigDB GO:BP membership, so a gene is not lost when its own GO:BP set fell
outside the size filter. A slim term is broad by design, so the 15-to-500 rule reads measured size.

```{r}
#| label: go-slim
slim_offspring <- AnnotationDbi::mget(
  GSEABase::ids(GSEABase::getOBOCollection(paths[["goslim"]])), GO.db::GOBPOFFSPRING,
  ifnotfound = NA
)
slim_offspring <- slim_offspring[!is.na(slim_offspring)]
go_genes <- membership |>
  filter(collection == "GOBP") |>
  with(split(gene, source_id))
slim_sets <- imap(slim_offspring, function(descendants, slim_id) {
  covered <- intersect(c(slim_id, descendants), names(go_genes))
  sort(intersect(unique(unlist(go_genes[covered], use.names = FALSE)), gene_universe))
})
slim_catalog <- tibble(
  theme_id = names(slim_sets),
  pathway = unname(AnnotationDbi::Term(GO.db::GOTERM[theme_id])),
  measured_size = lengths(slim_sets)
) |>
  transmute(
    set_id = paste("GO_Slim", toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", pathway)), sep = "|"),
    collection = "GO_Slim", pathway, source_id = theme_id,
    description = "GO Slim term: every measured gene under it in the GO:BP hierarchy",
    source_size = measured_size, measured_size,
    qualifies = measured_size >= 15 & measured_size <= 500
  )
names(slim_sets) <- slim_catalog$set_id
set_catalog <- bind_rows(set_catalog, slim_catalog)
sets <- c(sets, slim_sets[slim_catalog$set_id[slim_catalog$qualifies]])
c(slim_terms = nrow(slim_catalog), slim_testable = sum(slim_catalog$qualifies))
```

## Validation

Every set name is unique, every tested set meets its size rule, and every member is in the gene
universe.

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(set_catalog$set_id), !anyDuplicated(names(sets)),
  all(lengths(sets) >= 15), all(lengths(sets) <= 500),
  all(unlist(sets) %in% gene_universe)
)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary
collection_summary <- set_catalog |>
  summarise(
    n_in_source = n(), n_qualifying = sum(qualifies),
    median_measured = median(measured_size[qualifies]), .by = collection
  ) |>
  arrange(match(collection, c(collections, "GO_Slim")))
collection_summary
```

`r nrow(protein_map)` proteins map to `r length(gene_universe)` genes. `r length(sets)` sets
qualify for testing across `r nrow(collection_summary)` collections.

## Save

`gene_sets.rds` is read by every set-level step: set scores, module characterisation, set contrasts,
classification, trait associations and the overview figures.

```{r}
#| label: save
saveRDS(
  list(
    sets = sets, set_catalog = set_catalog, protein_map = protein_map,
    gene_universe = gene_universe
  ),
  file.path(out, "gene_sets.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
sheets <- list(
  collection_summary = collection_summary,
  set_catalog = set_catalog,
  protein_gene_map = protein_map,
  mapping_summary = mapping_summary
)
holds <- c(
  "Sets per collection in the source, sets that qualify, median measured size.",
  "Every set with its source and measured size and whether it qualifies (15 to 500).",
  "Every protein, its gene symbol, and the representative chosen per symbol.",
  "Proteins per mapping status."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "gene_sets.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
